claim: The Full Employment and Balanced Growth Act of 1978 (Public Law 95-523, October 27, 1978) did not first create the objectives. Section 108(a) amended Section 2A of the Federal Reserve Act's reporting provisions. The notes do not verify that it specifically replaced the 1977 second and third sentences, so that detail is unverified.

The report should state affirmatively, not just note the omission, that the 1977 Act lists three goals (maximum employment, stable prices, moderate long-term interest rates). It should also say that the Fed itself calls its mandate the 'dual mandate' because stable prices and maximum employment tend to produce moderate long-term interest rates. The Fed therefore treats moderate rates as a consequence of the other two goals, not a separate co-equal objective. The statutory text should not be para
passage: the Fed’s mandate for monetary policy is commonly known as the dual mandate
